detail: supported

It differs from [ACE0](16422-ace0.md) by using transformers and dense predictions, and from [InstantSplat](16423-splatt3r.md) and [Splatt3R](16423-splatt3r.md) by regressing points in the global coordinate frame without aligning dense pointmaps [S1, unofficial].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence in Source [S1]. The 'Notes' section explicitly states that the method 'Differs from ACE0: ... uses transformers ... predicts dense pointmaps' and 'Differs from InstantSplat and Splatt3R: regresses points in the global coordinate frame ... without aligning dense pointmaps'. These points are corroborated in the 'Passages' section, which details the use of transformers (ViT encoder/decoder) versus ACE0's CNN/MLP, the prediction of dense pointmaps versus ACE0's sparse ones, and the specific difference from InstantSplat/Splatt3R regarding regression in the global coordinate frame without aligning dense pointmaps.
supported

*   **Limitations:** Requires a large pretrained foundation model; finetuning is challenging as 3D foundation models are supervised by ground-truth 3D points difficult to obtain in unseen scenes [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method requires a large pretrained foundation model and that finetuning is challenging because these models are supervised by ground-truth 3D points which are difficult to obtain in unseen scenes. Source [S1] explicitly supports both parts of this claim: 1) It states, 'Our method leverages a pretrained foundation model as the neural scene representation.' 2) It explicitly states, 'Moreover, finetuning a pretrained foundation model such as DUSt3R is not easy. This is because these 3D foundation models are supervised by ground-truth 3D points that are difficult to obtain in unseen scenes.'
supported
*   **GPU Memory:** Runs on a 24GB consumer-level GPU for hundreds of images [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method runs on a 24GB consumer-level GPU for hundreds of images. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the notes section ('GPU memory requirement: runs on a 24GB consumer-level GPU for hundreds of images') and in the main text ('Our method can handle hundreds of images and run on a 24GB consumer-level GPU').
supported

*Note: $X_{i,j}$ denotes the pointmap of image $j$ in camera $i$'s coordinate frame in the base DUSt3R formulation, but ZeroGS uses Spann3R to regress directly into the global frame of the seed image without aligning pairwise dense pointmaps [S1, unofficial].*

The claim states that in the base DUSt3R formulation, $X_{i,j}$ denotes the pointmap of image $j$ in camera $i$'s coordinate frame. This is explicitly confirmed in Source [S1] under '3.1. Preliminaries', which states: 'DUSt3R predicts the corresponding pointmaps $(Xi,i , Xj,i )$ for each image, where Xi,j denotes the pointmap Xj expressed in camera i’s coordinate frame.' The claim also states that ZeroGS uses Spann3R to regress directly into the global frame of the seed image without aligning pairwise dense pointmaps. This is supported by the notes ('Differs from InstantSplat and Splatt3R: regresses points in the global coordinate frame of a seed image without aligning dense pointmaps') and the passage ('unlike InstantSplat and Splatt3R, our method regresses points in the global coordinate frame of a seed image without aligning the dense pointmaps'). Additionally, the passage notes that DUSt3R's post-processing aligns pairwise dense pointmaps to a global frame, which is time-consuming, implying ZeroGS avoids this specific alignment step by using the global frame regression of Spann3R.
supported
ZeroGS was proposed by researchers from Alibaba Group (AIBluefisher) [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that ZeroGS was proposed by researchers from Alibaba Group (AIBluefisher). The evidence supports this in two ways: 1) The project page URL provided in the text is 'aibluefisher.github.io/ZeroGS', directly linking the project name to the handle 'AIBluefisher'. 2) The text explicitly states 'In this work, we propose ZeroGS...', confirming that the authors of the paper (associated with the handle) are the proposers of the method.
supported

Unlike [ACE0](16422-ace0.md), which predicts sparse points using CNNs, ZeroGS predicts dense pointmaps and 3D Gaussians using transformers and optimizes the scene via rendering loss rather than reprojection error [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the 'Scene Sparsity' section that ACE0 predicts sparse pointmaps while ZeroGS predicts dense pointmaps and 3D Gaussian primitives. It also states that ACE0 uses 2D CNN and MLP, while ZeroGS uses transformers. Furthermore, the 'Objective Function' section notes that ZeroGS uses a rendering loss, whereas scenes are optimized by reprojection error in SfM (which ACE0 is compared against as a learning-based SfM method). All specific claims in the statement are directly supported by the text.
supported
*   **Memory Complexity:** Fits within 24GB GPU memory for hundreds of images [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method fits within 24GB GPU memory for hundreds of images. Source [S1] explicitly states in the notes: 'GPU memory requirement: runs on a 24GB consumer-level GPU for hundreds of images.' Additionally, the passage text confirms: 'Our method can handle hundreds of images and run on a 24GB consumer-level GPU.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
supported
*   **Training Buffer:** A collection of registered images and their associated poses and 3D Gaussians [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the 'Training Buffer' is a collection of registered images and their associated poses and 3D Gaussians. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes a pipeline where images are 'progressively registered and added to the training buffer' (Passage 1). It further details that the method uses Spann3R to 'predict 3D Gaussians' and computes 'coarse camera poses' which are then refined. The pipeline iteratively updates the buffer with new registered images, implying the buffer contains the images, their poses (computed via RANSAC/PnP and refinement), and the 3D Gaussians predicted for them to render images and compute loss. All components mentioned in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported

d. **Coarse Pose Estimation:** Compute coarse camera poses for $I_j$ using RANSAC and a Perspective-n-Point (PnP) solver on 2D-3D correspondences between the predicted pointmaps and the known geometry [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that coarse camera poses are computed for image $I_j$ using RANSAC and a PnP solver on 2D-3D correspondences between predicted pointmaps and known geometry. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the 'Method' section: 'We then use RANSAC and a PnP solver to obtain the initial camera poses based on 2D-3D correspondences.' It also notes in the notes section: 'Compute coarse camera poses using RANSAC and a PnP solver on 2D-3D correspondences from the predicted pointmaps.' The 'known geometry' refers to the 3D points predicted by the model (Spann3R) which serve as the 3D points for the PnP solver.
supported
*   **Spatial Feature Memory:** Used by the Spann3R backbone to store fused features for global coordinate regression [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that 'Spann3R proposes a feature fusion mechanism to predict pointmaps... in a global coordinate frame. It computes a fused feature ftG in the t-th training epoch from a spatial feature memory.' This confirms that the spatial feature memory is used by the Spann3R backbone to store fused features for regression in the global coordinate frame.
supported
*   **Memory Limits:** Aligning pairwise dense pointmaps to a global frame (as done in DUSt3R post-processing for >2 images) is time-consuming and can exceed GPU memory limits [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that aligning pairwise dense pointmaps to a global frame (as done in DUSt3R post-processing for >2 images) is time-consuming and can exceed GPU memory limits. Source [S1] explicitly states in the notes and the main text: 'DUSt3R's post-processing for >2 images aligns pairwise dense pointmaps to a global frame, which is time-consuming and can exceed GPU memory limits.' and 'When handling more than two images, DUSt3R uses a post-processing step to align the pairwise dense pointmaps to a global coordinate frame, which is time-consuming and can exceed the GPU memory limitation.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
supported
f. **Gaussian Prediction:** Predict 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G}_k$ for the scene using the same network [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the 'Method' section that 'We first use Spann3R as the scene regressor network to predict 3D Gaussians Gk and pointmaps Xk from an image pair.' This directly supports the claim that the network predicts 3D Gaussians.
supported
3.  **Rendering and Loss:** Rasterize the predicted 3D Gaussians using the refined poses to render images [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method rasterizes predicted 3D Gaussians using refined poses to render images. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the 'Method' section: 'Subsequently, we rasterize the 3D Gaussians with the refined camera poses to render images.' It also confirms that the Gaussians are predicted by Spann3R ('predict 3D Gaussians Gk') and that the poses are refined ('refine the coarse camera poses by minimizing a point-to-camera ray consistency loss'). Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
supported
*   **Batch Size:** Images are registered in batches rather than individually [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that images are registered in batches rather than individually. Source [S1] explicitly supports this in two places: 1) In the notes section, it states 'Register a batch of images at once instead of individually.' 2) In the main text under 'Image Registration', it states 'Instead of registering images individually in an incremental manner, our method registers a batch of images each time.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
supported
1.  **Seed Initialization:** Initialize the pipeline with a pretrained model (based on DUSt3R/Spann3R) and a single seed image $I_{seed}$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the pipeline is initialized with a pretrained model (based on DUSt3R/Spann3R) and a single seed image. The evidence explicitly supports this in multiple sections: 1) The 'Seed Initialization' note states: 'Initialize the pipeline from a pretrained model and one seed image, rather than an image pair.' 2) The main text under 'Seed Initialization' confirms: 'our method initializes from a pretrained model and only one seed image.' 3) The 'Method' section mentions using 'Spann3R' (which is based on DUSt3R) as the scene regressor network. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
